name: Letter-Case Modifier Construction

dimensions.form: Premodifying adjective phrase (often hyphenated) naming letter case.
dimensions.meaning: Signals lowercase vs uppercase interpretation of the modified label.
dimensions.function: Marks ordinary vs institutional/proper readings within NP structure.
dimensions.distribution: Premodifier of category labels and role nouns.

1.specialization: Encodes letter-case as a premodifier (small-c, big-D), specifying the intended interpretive status.

examples.note: Ordinary descriptive sense; not the institution.

relatedConstructions.notes: Realized as an adjectival pre-head modifier in nominals.

grounds.locator: Literal case contrast, as the comparison for the constructed modifier

projection.target: The compact modifier big-D in a big-D Democrat can disambiguate the label before its head. The full PP with a capital D can follow the label and express an equivalent literal contrast.
projection.evidence: The lexical meanings of capital and small supply the comparison. The position and interpretation contrast uses constructed forms rather than claims about regional frequencies.

curious.title: Small-c and big-D labels
curious.summary: A word like small-c or big-D placed before a label tells the reader which kind of meaning the label has.
curious.body: Putting small-c before a word tells you to read it in its ordinary, descriptive sense, not as the name of an institution. Putting big-D before a word does the opposite. In She is a big-D Democrat, the label points to the party, while small-c catholic in He's a small-c catholic points to the ordinary sense. The little modifier names a letter and whether it's capital or small. It works as a quick instruction about how to read the word that follows. The longer version puts a phrase with a capital D after the label.
curious.try: Pick a word you could write with a capital or a small first letter. How could you tell a reader which meaning you intend?

teacher.summary: Explains compact modifiers like small-c and big-D that tell a reader how to interpret a label.
teacher.explain: This is the compact form of letter-case specification. A premodifying adjective phrase, often hyphenated, names a letter and its case (small, big, little) and signals how to read the label that follows: ordinary or descriptive, versus institutional or party-affiliated. It sits before the head in the nominal, like other pre-head adjectival modifiers. The same contrast can be expressed with a full PP after the label, such as with a capital D. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional; it rests on dictionary definitions of capital and small, so treat these as constructed illustrations.
teacher.terms: This dictionary treats it as a metalinguistic modifier: a modifier about how a word is written, used to guide how it is read.

contrasts.text: She is a Democrat with a capital D.
contrasts.note: The full PP after the label expresses an equivalent contrast.
The compact modifier before the label.

watch_for: A learner might read small-c as describing size, when it names the case of the letter.
A learner might expect the modifier to come after the label, when the compact form sits before it.
teacher.activity: Write pairs of sentences that need a capital letter to show an institutional meaning and a small letter to show an ordinary one. Partners explain each sentence in their own words and then add the compact modifier before the label.
